status_reasons: UNSUPPORTED: "The way Edinburgh Art Festival describes itself, you can't walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or long-lost creative you've never heard of." — The source sentence ('You can't walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you've never heard of') is the reviewer's own observation about the experience of the festival. The article converts it into a claim about how the festival 'describes itself' — an attribution of self-presentation/branding that the source does not establish. Nothing in the source quotes festival marketing, curatorial statements, or programme copy.

UNSUPPORTED: 'It is the register the whole event chooses for itself — undiscovered archives, secret histories, the underground and the unheralded, one previously unknown name after another.' — This asserts intent/agency on the festival's part ('chooses for itself'). The source phrases — 'queer narratives, secret histories, undiscovered archives: the whole festival is a celebration of the underground and unheralded' — are the critic's characterization of what the festival contains, not evidence that the festival deliberately adopted this register as its own framing. The article states a motive/self-framing claim as settled.

UNSUPPORTED: 'The festival keeps its faith in clarity here.' — The source contains only the reviewer's personal conviction ('I think they have a duty... to tell them clearly'), and elsewhere the reviewer explicitly finds much of the festival unclear ('mind-meltingly indecipherable', 'way too knowingly obtuse', 'impossible to figure out how any of it fits together'). Attributing a 'faith in clarity' to the festival itself is not established — arguably contradicted — by the source. The article's very next sentence correctly reassigns the conviction to 'one person', but this opening sentence still asserts a festival-level stance as fact.
